page: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-128g-32vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with 12 shared vCPUs on an Intel x86_64 architecture, featuring 6 physical cores and hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. Graphics acceleration is delivered by two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs, offering a combined total of 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 700 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data shows average performance across standard compute and memory tasks, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 21080.54 and a PassMark CPU score of 20085.48. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 102.38 GB/sec for read operations and 53.61 GB/sec for write operations. In LLM inference tests, the server demonstrates top-tier performance for prompt processing, achieving 8665.1 tokens/sec on a small 135M model and 613.27 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds are rated as strong for the 7B model at 32.35 tokens/sec.

The shared CPU allocation presents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, dedicated CPU performance, though the high system memory density and dual-GPU configuration mitigate this for memory-bound tasks. Qualitatively, the server offers a balanced resource profile for GPU-accelerated workloads that do not require top-tier dedicated CPU cores but benefit from significant VRAM and system memory. This configuration is suitable for medium-scale LLM inference, graphics rendering, parallel data processing, and database operations.
